stories.headline: AMD agrees to buy Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2B in stock; Li becomes AMD chief scientist

key_facts.fact: On Sept. 28, 2026, AMD announced a definitive agreement to acquire World Labs, the AI model and research lab led by Fei-Fei Li.
key_facts.excerpt: SANTA CLARA, Calif., Sept. 28, 2026 – AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire World Labs, an AI model and research lab led by AI pioneer Dr. Fei-Fei Li.

key_facts.fact: The all-stock deal is valued at about $8.2 billion and is expected to close by the end of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals.
key_facts.excerpt: The all-stock transaction is valued at approximately $8.2 billion and is expected to close by the end of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.

key_facts.fact: Fei-Fei Li will join AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist, reporting to CEO Lisa Su.
key_facts.excerpt: Dr. Fei-Fei Li will join AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist, reporting to Dr. Lisa Su.

key_facts.fact: World Labs builds spatial-intelligence models that generate, reconstruct and simulate interactive 3D environments, plus technology for robotic learning and simulation.
key_facts.excerpt: World Labs develops spatial-intelligence models that generate, reconstruct and simulate interactive 3D environments from text, image and video inputs, as well as technology for robotic learning and simulation.

key_facts.fact: AMD had previously invested in World Labs, which raised $1 billion earlier in 2026; AMD plans to keep World Labs separate from its chipmaking business until closing.
key_facts.excerpt: The chipmaker, which previously invested in World Labs, said it's paying for the startup in stock... AMD plans to keep World Labs separate from its chipmaking business until the transaction closes later this year.

key_facts.fact: AMD and World Labs formed an inference-optimization and training partnership last year.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD and World Labs formed an inference optimization-and-training partnership last year, and ties have remained close.

key_facts.fact: World Labs says Justin Johnson and Ben Mildenhall will continue leading the team with Li inside AMD, building an open AI ecosystem spanning hardware, software and open models.
key_facts.excerpt: Justin Johnson and Ben Mildenhall will work with Fei-Fei to continue leading the World Labs team as it joins AMD to form a world leading frontier research organization.

sources.title: AMD to Acquire World Labs to Advance the Future of AI
AMD acquiring Fei-Fei Li's World Labs AI firm in deal worth $8.2B
AMD will acquire Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2 billion

stories.headline: Samsung affiliates commit $1B to Helix, the KKR-founded AI data-center and power company

key_facts.fact: On Sept. 29, 2026, six Samsung affiliates announced a combined $1 billion investment in Helix Digital Infrastructure, with Samsung Electronics putting in $500 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics to invest USD 500 million; five other affiliates investing the remainder... Samsung Electronics, Samsung C&T, Samsung SDS, Samsung SDI, Samsung Life Insurance and Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance today announced they are investing a combined USD 1 billion in Helix Digital Infrastructure

key_facts.fact: Helix, launched in June 2026 by KKR, covers hyperscale data center development, power generation, transmission and fiber networks, and is led by former AWS CEO Adam Selipsky.
key_facts.excerpt: Launched in June 2026, Helix is an AI-enabling infrastructure provider... including hyperscale data center development and operations, power generation... Helix is led by Adam Selipsky, former CEO of Amazon Web Services (AWS)

key_facts.fact: Samsung joins founding investors KKR, the Kuwait Investment Authority, Nvidia and US power company Vistra.
key_facts.excerpt: Alongside Samsung, KKR, the Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), NVIDIA, and US power company Vistra are also founding investors in Helix.

key_facts.fact: The $1 billion adds to the $10 billion already secured when the KKR-led consortium established Helix in June.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung commits $1B to AI infrastructure company Helix, adding to the $10B already secured when a KKR-led consortium including Nvidia established Helix in June

key_facts.fact: Helix plans to secure power capacity through direct investments and partnerships with energy developers including Vistra, calling power the biggest bottleneck in AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Recognizing that power availability is currently the greatest bottleneck in AI infrastructure, Helix plans to rapidly secure energy capacity through direct investments and strategic partnerships with major energy developers, including investor Vistra.

key_facts.fact: Samsung brings chips, data-center cooling via its FläktGroup subsidiary (acquired in 2025), and EPC construction via Samsung C&T.
key_facts.excerpt: delivers a comprehensive portfolio of data center cooling products and solutions... through FläktGroup, its data center HVAC specialist subsidiary acquired in 2025... Samsung C&T Engineering & Construction Group is actively driving the large-scale infrastructure projects as an engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contractor

sources.title: Samsung To Invest USD 1 Billion in AI Infrastructure Company Helix
Samsung Commits $1 Billion to AI Infrastructure Firm Backed by KKR, Nvidia

stories.headline: Nvidia in talks with insurers to protect lenders against neocloud defaults on chip-backed loans

key_facts.fact: Nvidia has held talks with insurance companies about shifting the risk of lending against its chips, the Financial Times reported on Sept. 29.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has held talks with insurance companies about shouldering the risks of lending against its chips

key_facts.fact: One proposed structure would insure lenders if a neocloud defaults and the Nvidia chips pledged as collateral cannot be resold for enough to repay the loan; the talks are early and may not produce deals.
key_facts.excerpt: One proposal under discussion involves insuring losses on loans to smaller cloud computing groups, often called neoclouds, if they default and the Nvidia chips pledged as collateral cannot be resold for enough to repay lenders. The conversations remain at an early stage and may not result in deals

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is working with broker Howden Re and has shared chip-depreciation and future compute-price data with at least one insurer; it is also exploring syndicating risk to hedge funds because deal sizes could exceed insurers' balance sheets.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has shared data on chip depreciation and expected future computing prices with at least one insurer. Another person said the company is working with broker Howden Re on a structure involving insurers, while also exploring ways to syndicate risk to hedge funds

key_facts.fact: Nvidia told the FT its AI infrastructure is "uniquely productive, durable and fungible."
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia told the FT that its AI infrastructure is "uniquely productive, durable and fungible," as the company works to broaden compute access beyond customers with Big Tech-sized balance sheets.

key_facts.fact: The effort extends an August partnership with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilize over $500 billion for AI infrastructure, and Nvidia's agreement to provide up to $105 billion in guarantees for an Ohio data center leased by an OpenAI affiliate.
key_facts.excerpt: In August, Nvidia partnered with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR on platforms designed to mobilize more than $500 billion of third-party capital for AI infrastructure... Nvidia has agreed to provide up to $105 billion in guarantees supporting land, power and shell buildout for an Ohio data center leased by an OpenAI affiliate.

sources.title: Nvidia turns to insurers to offset AI risks
Nvidia explores insurance-backed financing for AI chip customers
Nvidia Reportedly Turns To Insurers To De-Risk AI Chip Loans As Jensen Huang Pushes Beyond Big Tech

stories.headline: TSMC reportedly eyes Dallas for a second US chip hub that could top its $265B Arizona outlay

key_facts.fact: Taiwan's Economic Daily News reported TSMC is planning a second US manufacturing hub with as many as six advanced wafer fabs, with Dallas, Texas as a potential location; TSMC had not responded as of Sept. 28.
key_facts.excerpt: sources say the chipmaker is planning a second manufacturing hub that could include as many as six advanced wafer fabs, with Dallas, Texas emerging as a potential location... TSMC had not responded to a request for comment as of press time on September 28.

key_facts.fact: Because the new fabs would likely use more advanced nodes, total investment could exceed the $265 billion TSMC committed to Arizona.
key_facts.excerpt: As the new fabs would likely adopt more advanced nodes, total investment could exceed the US$265 billion committed to its Arizona complex.

key_facts.fact: The push reflects demand from Nvidia, Intel, AMD and Apple for US production, and Trump's renewed threat of tariffs of up to 200% on chipmakers that do not move manufacturing to the US.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC is considering the Texas campus partly in response to demand from major customers, including Nvidia, Intel, Advanced Micro Devices, and Apple, for domestic chip production. The report also cited US President Donald Trump's warnings that chipmakers could face tariffs of up to 200%

key_facts.fact: US customers made up about 75.64% of TSMC's revenue in the first half of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: US customers accounted for approximately 75.64% of TSMC's revenue in the first half of 2026, according to UDN

key_facts.fact: Supply-chain sources believe site evaluation is nearing its final stages, but TSMC's board has not decided and the company has made no official statement.
key_facts.excerpt: Supply-chain sources said they believed the site evaluation was nearing its final stages, though TSMC's board had not made a final decision.

key_facts.fact: TSMC is said to envision a 'southern semiconductor dual-core corridor' linking Arizona wafer manufacturing with Texas's chip ecosystem.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC is also said to be envisioning what it calls a "southern semiconductor dual-core corridor" linking Arizona and Texas.

sources.title: TSMC Reportedly Eyes Texas Expansion That Could Top US$265B; VIS-NXP Mulls Second Singapore Fab

stories.headline: Samsung Electro-Mechanics commits $5B to AI chip substrates, with customers co-funding capacity

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electro-Mechanics' board decided on Sept. 28 to invest a total of 6.78 trillion won in package-substrate capacity: 4.27 trillion won at its Sejong plant and 2.51 trillion won at its Vietnamese subsidiary.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electro-Mechanics (009150) decided at a board meeting on the 28th to invest 4.27 trillion won in expanding package substrate production at its Sejong plant, and will add 2.51 trillion won at its Vietnamese production subsidiary, for a total expansion of 6.78 trillion won.

key_facts.fact: The Sejong expansion makes FC-BGA substrates for AI accelerators, runs through May 2028, with mass production starting in September 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: invest 4.27 trillion won ($3,2 billion) in its Sejong plant through May 2028 to expand production of flip chip-ball grid array substrates, or FC-BGAs, which are used in AI accelerators and other high-performance chips. Mass production is scheduled to begin in September 2028.

key_facts.fact: Global big-tech customers are funding part of the capex and guaranteeing medium- to long-term volumes; local reports say Nvidia provided the largest share of trillions of won in advance payments, which the company has not confirmed.
key_facts.excerpt: Local media reports citing multiple industry officials said Nvidia and other big-tech customers had provided advance payments totaling trillions of won, with Nvidia accounting for the largest share. Samsung Electro-Mechanics has not confirmed those details.

key_facts.fact: The 4.27 trillion won package-substrate outlay is the largest single-product investment in the company's history, equal to 43.6% of its shareholders' equity.
key_facts.excerpt: The 4.27 trillion won package substrate expansion approved at the board meeting on the 28th is the largest investment tied to a single product in the company's history. The amount equals 43.6% of the 9.7973 trillion won in consolidated shareholders' equity recorded last year.

key_facts.fact: Since May the company has disclosed 3.32 trillion won in long-term contracts for silicon capacitors and AI-server MLCCs.
key_facts.excerpt: Since May, the company has disclosed 3.32 trillion won in long-term deals for silicon capacitors and AI-server multilayer ceramic capacitors

sources.title: Samsung Electro-Mechanics W6.78tr buildout gets customer backing
Samsung Electro-Mechanics to Invest 6.78 Trillion Won in AI Chip Substrates

stories.headline: Samsung Foundry targets HPC at 66% of its business by 2029, with 1.4nm mass production that year

key_facts.fact: At an investor presentation during Korea Premium Week 2026 on Sept. 29, Samsung foundry VP Noh Mi-jung said the unit aims to grow its customer base to about four times its 2017 level by 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: "We expect that figure to rise to about four times by 2029," the executive said at an investor presentation during Korea Premium Week 2026, held on the 29th at The Grand Lotte Seoul

key_facts.fact: High-performance computing was 5% of the foundry business in 2017, is 28% now, and is targeted at 66% by 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: HPC accounted for just 5% of the foundry business in 2017 and now stands at 28%. The company plans to raise that to 66% by 2029.

key_facts.fact: Samsung plans mass production of SF2P, its third-generation 2nm process, in 2028 and of SF1.4 (1.4nm) in 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics aims to begin mass production of SF2P, its third-generation 2-nanometer process, in 2028, followed by mass production of SF1.4, a 1.4-nanometer process, in 2029.

key_facts.fact: Its first Taylor, Texas fab will begin initial operations late this year, and a second Taylor fab is to break ground within the year, targeting mass production in 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: The company plans to begin initial operations at its first fab in Taylor, Texas, late this year. It also plans to break ground on a second Taylor fab within the year, targeting mass production in 2030.

sources.title: Samsung Foundry Aims to Quadruple Customers, Lift HPC Share to 66% by 2029

stories.headline: Crusoe revealed as developer of Google's wind-powered AI data center campus near Amarillo

key_facts.fact: On Sept. 28, 2026, Crusoe announced it is the developer of Google's data center campus under construction in Armstrong County, outside Amarillo, Texas.
key_facts.excerpt: CLAUDE, TX – September 28, 2026 – Crusoe, the AI factory company, today announced it is the developer of Google's data center campus under construction in Armstrong County outside of Amarillo.

key_facts.fact: The campus connects directly to Serena's Goodnight 1 wind farm (265.5 MW, operational) and Goodnight 2 (265.5 MW, under construction), with surplus power sent back to the grid.
key_facts.excerpt: The campus has a direct connection to Serena's adjacent Goodnight 1 (265.5 MW) wind farm, which is operational, and Goodnight 2 (265.5 MW) wind farm, which is currently under construction... When wind generation exceeds campus demand, surplus power is supplied back to the grid

key_facts.fact: The site uses closed-loop, non-evaporative liquid cooling to limit water use.
key_facts.excerpt: The project will utilize a closed-loop, non-evaporative liquid cooling system, which is designed to significantly limit the facility's water footprint

key_facts.fact: Construction began in June 2025 and has more than 5,500 workers on site daily.
key_facts.excerpt: Construction broke ground in June 2025 and is underway, with more than 5,500 skilled laborers on-site daily

key_facts.fact: CEO Chase Lochmiller said Crusoe's strategy is to build AI factories at the source of abundant, low-cost energy.
key_facts.excerpt: "Crusoe's strategy is to build AI factories directly at the source of abundant, low-cost energy – to both improve utilization of existing assets as well as catalyze new energy generation," said Chase Lochmiller

sources.title: Crusoe Developing Data Center Campus in Armstrong County, Texas
